title: Engine Electronic Control Unit — Connection and Routing of the Control Harness Channels

ata.title: Engine Fuel Control — Electronic Control Unit

abstract: Connection and routing of both engine electronic control harness channels, with the separation check along the fan case, the fire-rated clamp rule and the built-in test that closes the task.

sections.purpose: This task gives the procedure to route and connect both channels of the engine electronic control harness, to confirm the separation between the channels along the fan case and to do the control unit built-in test.
sections.job_setup_note: On a re-routed engine the two channels run on opposite sides of the fan case and the separation must be confirmed along the whole exposed length, not only at the ends. Only fire-rated clamps may be used inside the designated fire zone; a standard clamp fitted there invalidates the segregation argument and is not visible once the cowls are closed. The fire-rated sleeving is supplied cut to length and must not be spliced.
sections.procedure: 1. Confirm that the control unit is installed and that both connector faces are clean. 2. Fit the fire-rated sleeving over the section of each channel inside the designated fire zone. CAUTION: DO NOT SPLICE THE SLEEVING. A SPLICED LENGTH DOES NOT MEET THE FIRE RATING AND CANNOT BE SEEN ONCE THE COWLS ARE CLOSED. 3. Route channel A on the four o'clock side through its clamps. 4. Route channel B on the eight o'clock side through the support brackets, using a fire-rated clamp at every position inside the fire zone. 5. Confirm the minimum separation between the two channels along the whole exposed length with the separation gauge. WARNING: A SINGLE POINT BELOW THE MINIMUM SEPARATION FAILS THE INSTALLATION. MEASURE ALONG THE RUN, NOT ONLY AT THE ENDS. 6. Confirm that neither channel touches a fuel line, a flange or a hot surface at any point. 7. Renew the connector backshell on each channel. 8. Connect channel A and torque the coupling nut to the value in the figure. 9. Connect channel B and torque the coupling nut. 10. Fit the harness identification sleeves for the route standard fitted. 11. Do the control unit built-in test and confirm both channels report healthy. 12. Do the engine ground run called out in the figure and confirm no control fault is recorded. 13. Close the core cowl and the fan cowl doors.
sections.close_out: Record the route standard fitted, the clamp standard used and the built-in test result in the engine record. Confirm the harness identification sleeves match the route standard, because the engine change documentation depends on them. Report any position where the separation gauge could not be used.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Steps 4 and 5 apply in the re-routed form only on aircraft post MOD-148830.

safety_precautions: Confirm that the fuel system is isolated.
Do not use a standard clamp inside the designated fire zone.
Keep clear of the exhaust during the ground run.
